newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia says GDP to grow despite production slide.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia says GDP to grow despite production slide.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said he expected the economy to grow between three and four percent, in line with earlier government forecasts, despite a fall in industrial production so far this year.
Drnovsek told a news conference that industrial production represented only 30 percent of Slovenia's GDP. He did not name the other sectors.
"Growth in other economic areas shows that there will be a GDP rise of between three and four percent," he said.
In the first eight months of 1996 industrial output fell by 1.7 percent compared with the same period of 1995. Output in August was 2.7 percent lower than a year ago.
In May the government cut its GDP growth forecast to between three and four percent from five percent.
Drnovsek traced the decline in industrial output to the incomplete restructuring of Slovenian industry and the loss of markets in the former Yugoslavia.
He hoped that parliament would pass a government proposal that free extra money to help troubled companies before elections on November 10.
Drnovsek said he also considered interest rates too high but he noted that was a matter for the central bank.
"Although high interest rates stimulate savings, they are becoming an obstacle to faster economic development," he said. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
